column2: [intro]
When I wake up in the morning, I'm not super glam,
Sequins and makeup? Not my jam, ma’am.
But as soon as I show up, everyone’s in awe,
And all I want to do is hide—it's just a flaw.
I’m a pop star, the world adores,
But there’s one thing that still makes me sore.
People see me as too perfect, it’s true,
But I’m tired of the seams and what they construe.
I’m tired of smiling all the time for the cam,
My life’s not all sparkles and glam.
I want to be real, without masks or glitz,
The worth of a person isn’t in their bits.
It’s the Couture Show, but I don’t agree,
It’s my flaws I want to show, let them be.
I’m not a doll; I’m just me,
And if they see the seams, I’m fine, I’m free.
[ solo ]
It’s the Couture Show, but I don’t agree,
It’s my flaws I want to show, let them be.
I’m not a doll; I’m just me,
And if they see the seams, I’m fine, I’m free.
[outro]
